# Bunraku documentation

> Where every Bunraku document lives, from user guides and current references to accepted decisions, future specifications, and generated navigation.

## Decisions

- [ADR-001: Runtime - Bun + TypeScript, Node-compatible core](docs/decisions/ADR-001-runtime.md): **Status:** accepted
- [ADR-002: License, AGPL-3.0-or-later](docs/decisions/ADR-002-license.md): **Status:** accepted
- [ADR-003: Distribution - single executable + self-updater; installer later](docs/decisions/ADR-003-distribution.md): **Status:** accepted
- [ADR-005: Canonical superset model + escrow envelope](docs/decisions/ADR-005-canonical-model.md): **Status:** accepted
- [ADR-006: AI - BYOK + local, and an agent built for weak models](docs/decisions/ADR-006-ai-and-agent.md): **Status:** accepted
- [ADR-007: Renderer policy (shell vanilla, per-app freedom, chat surfaces re-evaluated at spec time)](docs/decisions/ADR-007-renderer-policy.md): **Status:** accepted · 2026-07-05 **Context owners:** the shell (`src/ui/`), every app folder, the future Table Read and agent surfaces
- [ADR-008: React UI layer for structural rendering safety](docs/decisions/ADR-008-react-ui.md): **Status:** accepted · 2026-07-05 **Supersedes:** ADR-007's "decide per chat surface later." ADR-007's engine rule is carried forward unchanged and hardened here.
- [ADR-009: Distinct origin for test-bench execution](docs/decisions/ADR-009-sandbox-origin.md): **Status:** accepted in design; packaged-host proof BLOCKED; 2026-07-09 **Context owners:** `src/sandbox/lua/`, `src/sandbox/regex/`, `src/ui/server.ts`, `src/ui/sandbox-host.ts`, desktop entries **Audit IDs:** SANDBOX-001 (Plan 017)
- [ADR-010: Shared semantic content capabilities](docs/decisions/ADR-010-content-capabilities.md): **Status:** accepted, 2026-07-25
- [ADR-011: Exhaustive runtime schemas at canonical boundaries](docs/decisions/ADR-011-runtime-boundary-schemas.md): **Status:** accepted, 2026-07-26
- [ADR-012: Macro evaluation is a closed-world interpreter, not a second script sandbox](docs/decisions/ADR-012-macro-evaluation-boundary.md): **Status:** accepted, 2026-08-23 (proposed 2026-07-26) **Context owners:** `src/core/preset/macros/`, `src/sandbox/`, a future `src/core/macros/` **Supersedes nothing. Constrains:** any implementation of the macro engine
- [ADR-013: The scene's wings and tabs get slots in the one slot registry](docs/decisions/ADR-013-wing-slots.md): **Status:** proposed, 2026-10-12 (awaiting review) **Context owners:** `src/extensions/slot-registry.ts`, `src/ui/_shared/theme-slot.tsx`, `src/ui/apps/scenes/` **Supersedes nothing. Extends:** the slot list in the theme-package contract

## Guide

- [Convert a card](docs/guide/converting.md): Take a card you have in one app's format and ship it out in another, and see plainly what crosses and what stays behind.
- [Edit a piece](docs/guide/editing.md): Open a piece on the Workbench, change it through the Grid or Steps view, and save your draft explicitly before you close the tab.
- [Export a piece](docs/guide/exporting.md): Send a piece out of Vaudeville Studios through the character editor's Export button, or a staged batch through the Press, and see exactly what travels before anything downloads.
- [Frequently asked questions](docs/guide/faq.md): Straight answers on where your files live, what a convert actually keeps or drops, which apps Bunraku reads and writes, and whether converting or editing a card can damage it.
- [Get started](docs/guide/getting-started.md): Install Bunraku, get through the four-question setup wizard, learn the rooms the Dock puts in front of you, and bring your first file into the Library.
- [Import a file](docs/guide/importing.md): Bring a card, lorebook, persona, or regex set into the Library by dropping it on the shelves or clicking Import, and see exactly what the receipt keeps before anything is written.
- [Browse the Library](docs/guide/library.md): Browse every deck's cards in rows or a grid, switch any deck's section to another view, use each card's own tools, and stage one piece or many for a single send to the Workbench.
- [Build a lorebook](docs/guide/lorebooks.md): Add entries to a lorebook, give each one the keywords that trigger it, and decide where it lands in the assembled prompt.
- [Create and manage personas](docs/guide/personas.md): Build a persona on the Workbench from identity and sections or flat text, set where it injects and what it links to, and know the few places it behaves differently from a character.
- [Agnai](docs/guide/platforms/agnai.md): Bringing Agnai character JSON and memory books into Bunraku and back out.
- [Backyard](docs/guide/platforms/backyard.md): Bringing Backyard.ai's two character card shapes, the older flat JSON export and the modern .byaf archive, into Bunraku and back out.
- [Chub](docs/guide/platforms/chub.md): Bringing Chub character cards and lorebooks into Bunraku and back out.
- [Lumiverse](docs/guide/platforms/lumiverse.md): Bringing Lumiverse character cards, expression archives, personas, and regex scripts into Bunraku and back out.
- [Marinara](docs/guide/platforms/marinara.md): Bringing Marinara-Engine regex scripts and personas into Bunraku and back out.
- [NovelAI](docs/guide/platforms/novelai.md): Bringing NovelAI lorebooks into Bunraku and back out.
- [Pygmalion](docs/guide/platforms/pygmalion.md): Bringing Pygmalion's classic flat character JSON into Bunraku and back out.
- [Platforms](docs/guide/platforms/README.md): A short map of every platform Bunraku reads and writes today, what each one hands over, and which guide page to open first.
- [RisuAI](docs/guide/platforms/risu.md): Bringing RisuAI .charx cards, lorebooks, and regex scripts into Bunraku and back out.
- [RoleCall](docs/guide/platforms/rolecall.md): Bringing RoleCall character cards and lorebooks into Bunraku and back out.
- [SillyTavern](docs/guide/platforms/sillytavern.md): Bringing SillyTavern character cards and worldbooks into Bunraku and back out.
- [User guide](docs/guide/README.md): A map of Bunraku's rooms and links to every guide page, setup, importing, browsing, editing, personas, lorebooks, regex sets, converting, exporting, and platform notes.
- [Edit a regex set](docs/guide/regex.md): Write find-and-replace rules into a set, choose where and in what order each one runs, and check what a rule actually does before you save it.
- [Security and privacy](docs/guide/security.md): What keeps your content and your keys on your machine, why a downloaded card cannot run code on its own, and the few places where a protection is partial and we say so.
- [Troubleshoot common problems](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md): Work out why the Studio would not open, why a card would not import, why a convert dropped something, or why an export looks wrong, using plain recovery steps.

## Reference

- [Architecture](docs/reference/architecture.md): The whole engine: the hub-and-spoke canonical model, escrow, the adapter contract, detection, folders-as-schema, bundles, and the CLI.
- [The audit suite](docs/reference/audits.md): Runnable UI audits under `scripts/audit/`. They drive the real app in a real browser against a scratch studio seeded through the real adapters, and they **enumerate the live app at runtime**: the room list comes from the dock, deck and view
- [CLI reference](docs/reference/cli.md): Every bunraku command and flag, verified against src/cli.ts and src/cli-io.ts, with usage, behavior, JSON output shapes, and exit codes.
- [Component catalog](docs/reference/components.md): Auto-generated by `scripts/hooks/component-catalog.ts` from exported UI entries under pre-commit gate (`--check`) fails the commit when this file drifts from the real exports.
- [Bundles](docs/reference/concepts/bundles.md): How a character card's embedded lorebook splits into two linked canonical entities, a CanonicalCharacter and a CanonicalLorebook joined by knowledgeRefs, extracted on import and re-embedded on export.
- [The canonical superset model](docs/reference/concepts/canonical-model.md): The one hub every format converts through, a versioned entity wrapper whose body is the union of what real formats express, governed by the superset rule that a field earns a canonical slot only when a real wire format serializes it.
- [The embedded character_book](docs/reference/concepts/character-book.md): A card's embedded character_book is extracted into a standalone linked lorebook on import and re-embedded into the target format's book slot on export.
- [Detection and the registry](docs/reference/concepts/detection.md): How bunraku sniffs a file's format from its content, scores each adapter's confidence, keeps the single best match above a threshold, and stops any detector from claiming another entity kind's files.
- [Escrow and round-trip](docs/reference/concepts/escrow-and-roundtrip.md): How the escrow envelope preserves same-format fields and keeps cross-format conversion loss contained by design.
- [Concept: the persona editor](docs/reference/concepts/persona-editor.md): The {{user}} sheet, wearing the CHARACTER editor's chassis on purpose (the kinship ruling, 2026-07-12): the same `.bento` three-column grid, `BentoCard` tiles, and `.lcard`/`.portrait` face plate from `editor-styles`. Source: `src/ui/apps/w
- [Concept: the regex editor](docs/reference/concepts/regex-editor.md): The Workbench surface for authoring a regex set. Source: `src/ui/apps/workbench/regex/` (one concept per file: `set-editor` chassis, `rule-toc`, `rule-page`, `phase-picker`, `fine-print`, ops in `session.ts`). Built by transcription from th
- [Concept: the regex engine](docs/reference/concepts/regex-engine.md): How bunraku actually RUNS a regex set. Source of truth: `src/core/regex/` (pure, no side effects). The entity it operates on is [entities/regex.md](../entities/regex.md); per-platform field/phase truth lives in `src/core/regex/capabilities.
- [Concept: safe content rendering (the render toggle)](docs/reference/concepts/safe-rendering.md): Character fields carry authored markup: descriptions and greetings are Markdown, creator notes arrive as HTML, and short facts (version, creator, license) are plain text. The editor and the read-only inspector render that markup so a field 
- [Concept: the tag taxonomy](docs/reference/concepts/tag-taxonomy.md): Character tags arrive as free strings from every source format (`discovery.tags` is `string[]`); no format carries a category on the wire. The editor still colors each tag chip by KIND, so a pure classifier decides which category a tag stri
- [Character entity](docs/reference/entities/character.md): The canonical superset entity for a roleplay character: every CharacterBody field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
- [Dice entity](docs/reference/entities/dice.md): The canonical piece for something a person rolls, made once and used anywhere. One kind with three types, a roll, a table or a pool, all rolled by the same dice math with randomness the caller hands in.
- [Formula entity](docs/reference/entities/formula.md): The canonical piece for a saved macro expression, such as a word count over the chat plus a roll, made once and run anywhere. A tool can run one; it runs on a copy of the turn's macro context and is refused when it would change anything.
- [Drawing entity](docs/reference/entities/htmldoc.md): The canonical HTML-document entity - a page the agent draws, kept as a studio piece so it can be named, edited, grouped and reopened; and the seal that renders it without ever running it.
- [Lorebook entity](docs/reference/entities/lorebook.md): The canonical superset entity for a lorebook (world info): every LorebookBody and LorebookEntry field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
- [Pack entity](docs/reference/entities/pack.md): The canonical studio entity for a reusable expression/sprite pack: every PackBody field, its type, and its meaning.
- [Persona entity](docs/reference/entities/persona.md): The canonical superset entity for a user persona: every PersonaBody field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
- [Preset entity](docs/reference/entities/preset.md): The canonical superset entity for a chat-completion prompt-manager preset: every PresetBody field, its type, the formats that produce it, and its meaning.
- [Prompt format entity](docs/reference/entities/promptformat.md): The canonical piece for SillyTavern instruct and context templates, kept whole under ST's own field names, and what reads it (nothing yet).
- [Quick-reply set entity](docs/reference/entities/quickreply.md): The canonical piece for SillyTavern quick-reply sets, a named page of buttons that send prepared text, kept as label and message per button with every other wire field escrowed, and linked from presets.
- [Entities](docs/reference/entities/README.md): Index of the canonical content kinds (character, lorebook, persona, pack, preset, Script Sheet, regex, quick-reply set, tool, dice, formula, tracker, prompt format, drawing), how each is one folder described once in its kind.ts, and links to each one's field reference and the shapes they share.
- [Regex entity](docs/reference/entities/regex.md): The canonical find/replace-script entity for a portable regex set: every RegexRule field, its type, the platforms that produce it, and its meaning.
- [Script Sheet entity](docs/reference/entities/scriptsheet.md): The canonical piece for a Script Sheet, RoleCall's single-instruction writing setup, kept as a name, one instruction and optional samplers. It is its own kind in the Writing family with presets: a scene uses it in the same slot, it shares the Writing deck, and it reads as the preset it sends.
- [Skill entity](docs/reference/entities/skill.md): The canonical piece for instructions the model gets only when they matter, such as how to run a sword fight. A skill is a prompt that fires like a lore entry, on the lorebook's own trigger fields and matcher, or always, or while the model has it open. A scene links skills; the ones on in a turn ride as one Skills block at the preset's skills marker, never dropped by the budget.
- [Tool entity](docs/reference/entities/tool.md): The canonical piece for a tool a model may call while it writes, kept as data with no code. A scene links the tools it offers, and each call runs one first-party action, a roll, a linked dice piece, a linked formula or a record, through the scene's existing tool loop. Every connection takes tools except models that refuse them, and a server's refusal is reported plainly, never retried without them.
- [Tracker entity](docs/reference/entities/tracker.md): The canonical piece for state a scene keeps, such as a character's health or a party's roster: named typed fields, kept as swipe-safe scene state, shown to the model every turn, readable by macros, and updated by the model through one tool. A scene links the trackers it keeps. Fields may carry icons and take a number's top from another field, a tracker has a change style, and a read answers what each reply changed; the backend, the Workbench editor, the Messenger's Trackers panel (linking, values and the person's own edits) and the change visuals under each reply are built.
- [Add a format adapter](docs/reference/extending/add-a-format.md): Every format converts through one canonical superset model, never format to format directly; adding a format is one adapter, and it touches no other format and no core code (`architecture.md`, "The one idea: hub and spoke"). This page is th
- [Make a theme](docs/reference/extending/make-a-theme.md): How to author a Bunraku theme package, a manifest that picks host-built layout variants for 30 surfaces and sets a checked palette, fonts, frame shape, motion and accent behavior, and can go further with one checked stylesheet, its own fonts and images, and content in named slots, with a copy-paste starter.
- [Add a content kind](docs/reference/extending/new-kind.md): How to add a new kind of piece (like presets or lorebooks): one folder under src/entities with its schema, decoder and kind.ts descriptor, then bun run kinds. Lists of kinds, labels, decks, decoders, storage folders, New actions, links, names and picture paths all read the generated seam. A completeness test names anything still missing, and a guard test fails on a new hand-written kind list.
- [Agnai format](docs/reference/formats/agnai.md): Agnai (Agnaistic) is a browser/self-hosted AI roleplay app with its own native JSON character shape. It is not Tavern-lineage: instead of a flat description block, its persona is structured, a `kind` plus an

- [Marinara format](docs/reference/formats/marinara.md): How the Marinara-Engine adapters map regex scripts, personas, lorebooks, and presets through the canonical model.

- [Pygmalion format](docs/reference/formats/pygmalion.md): How the Pygmalion adapter detects, maps, and round-trips the classic flat five-field character JSON and its PNG chara chunk through the canonical model.
- [Formats](docs/reference/formats/README.md): Every format bunraku reads and writes. A **format** is a folder in `src/formats/<name>/`; the loader discovers it automatically (see [../architecture.md](../architecture.md)). Each format family gets one
- [RisuAI format](docs/reference/formats/risu.md): How the RisuAI adapter family detects, maps, and round-trips .charx character cards, a native lorebook export, and regex script sets through the canonical model.
- [RoleCall to SillyTavern presets](docs/reference/formats/rolecall-to-sillytavern.md): What converts mechanically when a RoleCall preset becomes a SillyTavern preset, what Kit reports about the parts that do not, and the four patterns for finishing those by hand.
- [RoleCall format](docs/reference/formats/rolecall.md): How the RoleCall adapter family maps character cards, lorebooks, personas, regex scripts, and presets through the canonical model.
- [SillyTavern format](docs/reference/formats/sillytavern.md): How the SillyTavern adapter family detects, maps, and round-trips Character Card V1/V2/V3 cards and world info books through the canonical model.
- [vaud-json format](docs/reference/formats/vaud-json.md): How the vaud-json adapter serializes the canonical character entity straight to plain JSON with no wire translation, and why it always wins detection on its own files.
- [Glossary](docs/reference/glossary.md): Words that mean something particular in Bunraku, and the folder that owns each one. Read this before searching by name: several words here mean two different things, and a few folders are not what their names suggest. For where a specific f
- [Kit reference](docs/reference/kit/README.md): Kit's conversational runtime, semantic content capabilities, and change-draft lifecycle.
- [Kit content tools](docs/reference/kit/tools.md): Kit's shared workflow discovery, traversable results, semantic drafts, and Bunraku docs query.
- [reference/macro-engine](docs/reference/macro-engine.md): RoleCall's macro engine, ported under src/core/macros/ inside the closed world ADR-012 allows. It parses macro templates and evaluates them against a value-only context, producing expanded text plus segments that trace each rendered span back to the authored characters behind it, the contract the editable preview stands on. It behaves as RoleCall's engine does at the pinned commit, proven by a parity test over all 179 entries of RoleCall's own characterization corpus, recorded from RoleCall, plus RoleCall's ported processor and handler tests. Where ADR-012 requires, it differs: the clock, randomness, locale and time zone come from the context, and evaluation is bounded so no cut-off value is stored; four RoleCall families and its interceptors are left out. Callers are the ADR-012 list, now including chat display; codecs and adapters never evaluate, and macro text stays opaque payload at every import and conversion boundary.
- [Platform native fields (verified research)](docs/reference/platform-native-fields.md): Source of truth for building each platform's native-field schema (platforms/<key>.ts). Fields verified against each platform's real exported format. Confidence + open questions are honest per platform. A native field

- [SillyTavern macro syntax and operators](docs/reference/platforms/sillytavern/macro-operators.md): Complete operational guide to SillyTavern macro parsing, argument forms, nesting, scoped content, conditionals, flags, comments, escaping, variable identifiers, shorthand operators, return values, and legacy markers.

- [SillyTavern authoring source coverage](docs/reference/platforms/sillytavern/source-coverage.md): Path-level coverage map from the pinned SillyTavern-Docs tree to Bunraku platform references, with individual inclusion verdicts and no wildcard exclusions for authoring material.
- [SillyTavern World Info authoring](docs/reference/platforms/sillytavern/world-info.md): Operational model of SillyTavern lorebooks, including book attachment, keyword and vector activation, entry selection, prompt placement, recursion, groups, outlets, and budgets.
- [bunraku documentation](docs/reference/README.md): This is the reference documentation for **bunraku**, the Vaudeville Studios converter for AI-roleplay content. It is **docs-as-code**: it lives in the repo, is versioned with the code, and is kept true by
- [Scene state](docs/reference/scene-state.md): What a scene remembers beyond its text, kept so that every way of changing the shown history (a new version of a reply, choosing a version, cutting, restoring, forking) leaves it where the history says. A piece of state is a
- [Safe archive handling: .charx and .byaf](docs/reference/security/archives.md): How bunraku bounds a .charx or .byaf ZIP before and after inflation to resist a zip bomb, and where entry names are (and are not yet) checked for path traversal before they can become a filesystem write or a re-exported archive path.
- [Security threat model and defense layers](docs/reference/security/README.md): The assets bunraku protects, the untrusted inputs it faces, and each defense layer with its honest tested or scaffolded status.
- [ReDoS defense in the regex engine](docs/reference/security/regex-safety.md): Vaud parses every card-authored find pattern into an AST, screens it for catastrophic-backtracking shapes before it is ever compiled, refuses the dangerous ones with an exact culprit span, and surfaces the rejection reason as plain text in two places, with the coverage gaps in that screen documented here.
- [Remote access: Tailscale and LAN](docs/reference/security/remote-access.md): How bunraku lets you reach the studio from another device over a private Tailscale link or the local network, and the gates that keep everyone else out. Two listeners (trusted loopback, untrusted sidecar-fed), an owner-only Tailscale gate, and a connect-code + per-device-approval LAN gate. Off by default; driven entirely from Settings, never a terminal.
- [Safe rendering: sanitizing card HTML and CSS](docs/reference/security/safe-rendering.md): Specifies exactly what DOMPurify allows and strips on the two surfaces that render card-authored HTML and CSS, the sealed iframe and scoped CSP the riskier surface adds on top, and what is proven only at the string level versus what is not measured at all.
- [The Lua script sandbox](docs/reference/security/script-sandbox.md): How bunraku runs an untrusted card script in a terminable worker on a distinct loopback origin, behind a versioned value-only wire protocol and resource budgets that clamp downward only, with an honest account of what is enforced versus what is not yet measured.
- [Secrets, provider credentials, and local API authority](docs/reference/security/secrets-and-keys.md): How Kit encrypts BYOK provider configurations, constrains provider egress, and how the Studio gates its local API with a per-launch bearer plus Host and Origin checks.
- [Cards and files as untrusted input](docs/reference/security/untrusted-content.md): Cards, PNGs, and zip containers are parsed once into the canonical model without ever executing a card-authored script, and a cross-format conversion carries only the portable body, so one app's scripts and payloads never reach another app's file.
- [The token meter](docs/reference/token-meter.md): A token counter that learns every model from the usage its replies report. It lives in time. The scene turn loop feeds it: after each reply is committed, reported. A turn that used tool rounds is skipped, because its usage covers more than 
- [The visual app (bunraku ui)](docs/reference/ui.md): uses. Optional remote listeners are separately enabled and gated. One engine, two shells - no format logic exists in the UI layer.
- [Updates and version rollback](docs/reference/updates.md): The Updates settings tab, a version timeline built from each release's commit log, and a one-button switch that updates OR rolls back. How the switch works for a source checkout vs an installed build, and the safety rails (refuse a dirty tree, single-flight, restart-outcome marker, refuse a data-losing rollback). Off-network except a button-press GitHub read.

## Top level

- [Vision](docs/01-VISION.md): Simple for simple folk, an absolute unit for power users. Concretely, four people:
- [Architecture](docs/02-ARCHITECTURE.md): Bunraku is a Bun and TypeScript application rooted in `src/`. The canonical engine is shared by three surfaces: the command-line interface, the loopback React Studio, and Kit's terminal interface. No surface owns a private format conversion
- [Conventions](docs/03-CONVENTIONS.md): These are the repository's binding implementation rules. They describe current enforced practice, not an idealized future toolchain.
- [Format support matrix](docs/FORMAT-SUPPORT.md): Auto-generated from live adapters (`bun run scripts/format-matrix.ts`). Canonical schema version: **1**. Generated: 2026-10-29.
- [Documentation](docs/README.md): Where every Bunraku document lives, from user guides and current references to accepted decisions, future specifications, and generated navigation.
